title: Frank Slide
description: Explore Frank Slide, then answer a four-question quiz.
overviewDescription: Visit Frank Slide on the map, read about the 1903 rock avalanche, and answer four questions to record your discoveries.

activity.introduction: Start with the map to find Frank Slide and explore Turtle Mountain. Opening Frank Slide records the checkpoint that unlocks the quiz; opening Turtle Mountain adds a separate journal discovery.

mapFirst.heading: Explore the map first
mapFirst.description: Use the button below to open the expedition map and explore the Frank Slide and Turtle Mountain points. The map will fly to the site, then switch to plane mode. Return here after opening Frank Slide to take the quiz.

quiz.heading: Frank Slide quiz
quiz.lockedDescription: Find and select the Frank Slide point on the map first. The four-question quiz will unlock here once that checkpoint is recorded.

complete.title: Quiz complete!
complete.description: Your Frank Slide map discovery and quiz answers are recorded in your expedition journal.

frank-slide-quiz-event.prompt: What event is known as the Frank Slide?

options.turtle-mountain-rock-avalanche: A rock avalanche from Turtle Mountain
options.river-flood: A flood from the Crowsnest River
options.forest-fire: A wildfire that burned the town

frank-slide-quiz-event.correct: That's right! Part of Turtle Mountain collapsed in a rock avalanche.
frank-slide-quiz-event.tryAgain: Not quite. Think about the mass of rock that came down from Turtle Mountain.

frank-slide-quiz-mountain.prompt: Which mountain collapsed during the event?
frank-slide-quiz-mountain.correct: That's right! The rock avalanche came from Turtle Mountain.
frank-slide-quiz-mountain.tryAgain: Not quite. The mountain is beside the community of Frank.

frank-slide-quiz-date.prompt: On what date did the Frank Slide occur?
frank-slide-quiz-date.correct: That's right! The Frank Slide occurred on April 29, 1903.
frank-slide-quiz-date.tryAgain: Not quite. The event took place in the spring of 1903.

frank-slide-quiz-location.prompt: In which Alberta region is Frank Slide located?
frank-slide-quiz-location.correct: That's right! Frank Slide is in Crowsnest Pass in southwestern Alberta.
frank-slide-quiz-location.tryAgain: Not quite. Frank Slide is in the Rocky Mountain region of southwestern Alberta.

crowsnestPass.title: Crowsnest Pass
crowsnestPass.description: Crowsnest Pass crosses the Rocky Mountains between southwestern Alberta and southeastern British Columbia. Mountain slopes, lakes, and forested valleys surround this route through the mountains.
crowsnestPass.imageAlt: Mountain landscape at Crowsnest Pass, with turquoise lakes, a winding highway, forested slopes, and snow-streaked peaks beneath clouds.

lundbreckFalls.title: Lundbreck Falls
lundbreckFalls.description: Lundbreck Falls is a waterfall on the Crowsnest River near Lundbreck in southwestern Alberta. The river drops about 12 metres over a rocky ledge.
lundbreckFalls.imageAlt: Water cascading over a broad rocky ledge at Lundbreck Falls, with trees and a railway bridge in the background.

poi.description: On April 29, 1903, part of Turtle Mountain collapsed and a rock avalanche swept across the valley near the mining community of Frank.

turtleMountain.title: Turtle Mountain
turtleMountain.description: Turtle Mountain rises to about 2,210 m above Crowsnest Pass. At 4:10 a.m. on April 29, 1903, part of its east face broke away in the rock avalanche known as the Frank Slide.
turtleMountain.trailDescription: An informal route from near Blairmore climbs a steep shoulder to North Peak, and a hiking path connects South and Third Peaks. It is exposed, can be hard to follow, and includes scrambling and route-finding. Treat it as a demanding alpine outing for experienced hikers, not a maintained beginner trail.
turtleMountain.monitoringDescription: Alberta Geological Survey monitoring work has included a weather station, webcam, crack meters, tilt meters, and other sensors on South Peak to track movement. A 2018 government report also documented two blue emergency barrels near the weather station, with a radio, flashlight, blankets, water, first aid, cooking gear, and emergency food for stranded hikers.
turtleMountain.safetyNote: The emergency supplies are for unexpected survival situations, not a substitute for your own mountain gear. Check local access and weather before setting out, and do not disturb monitoring equipment.
